C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND.Summary: Make re-pairing an extension that already holds a live credential a distinct, confirmed operation instead of a silent token replacement.
C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND.Problem: POST /ext/pair generates a fresh secret and overwrites the stored credential under the client-declared extension id without checking whether that id is already paired or enabled, and without requiring knowledge of the existing secret. In debug builds the request is auto-approved, so a local process can re-key an enabled extension — its own or any id it names — with no user decision; in release builds the confirmation dialog describes a first pairing and does not tell the user that approving replaces the live key of an already-paired extension. Either way the previous token holder is displaced and the requester gains the id under its existing capability grants (verified finding F-006 debug-pairing-silently-rekeys-extension, security run be2f52f880bc; evidence live_server.rs pairing handler and debug auto-approve branch, auth.rs credential store).
C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND.Relationship: Lineage: same smart-review security run (be2f52f880bc) as C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE, which added RouteCapability gating on the incoming data routes and the honest pairing grant description. This change hardens the pairing route itself — the one incoming route that mints credentials — and must keep the C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE gate and grant wording intact. It complements C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH: after an approved rebind the previous token must fail validation exactly like a revoked one. The re-enable-after-failed-revocation finding (F-007) is a separate change and is not covered here. Sibling draft: C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING.

Goals.Goal: Pairing against an extension id that already holds a stored credential succeeds only when the request presents the prior secret, or after an explicit trust reset through the UI (a verified revocation such as disable) removed the stored secret.

The approval dialog distinguishes replacement from first pairing: it names the already-paired extension and states that approving replaces its live key; nothing is overwritten before an approval decision.

Debug auto-approval stays test-only: outside the Rust test harness no build approves pairing, or replaces a live key, without a user decision; when a rebind is not confirmed, the existing secret remains valid and no new secret is issued.
After an approved rebind the previous token is fenced on every incoming route; first-time pairing keeps its current behavior, response shape and grant description.

Constraints.Constraint: Exact write scope: src-tauri/src/m045_ext/live_server.rs and src-tauri/src/m045_ext/tests.rs only. No changes to auth.rs, registry, mod.rs commands, renderer files, manifests or CI; the has-existing-credential check is derived from the existing auth lookup functions.

Security boundaries: the prior-secret comparison is constant time; no log line, error message or response ever contains secret material; the loopback-only binding and Bearer model are unchanged; a refused rebind leaks no credential material and discloses no more than the pairing state the route already implies.

C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE lineage: RouteCapability gating of the data routes, pairing_grant_description wording for first pairing, and the C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH identity/epoch fencing of stream routes survive unchanged; re-pairing must not widen or bypass the manifest capability gate, and the rebind dialog must not grant wording the manifest does not declare.

The fix direction follows the verified finding: explicit confirmation for pairing and for replacing a live key, with automation kept inside the isolated test environment. PairRequest/PairResponse wire changes are additive; existing fields keep their names and meaning.
No version change, release, publication or deploy is authorized by this specification.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Redesigning the first-pairing UX, the extension gallery, or adding a new trust-reset surface beyond the existing disable command.
The re-enable path that reuses a surviving token after failed revocation (F-007) — a separate change.
Mac App Store builds, the extension registry/epoch design, manifest format changes and dependency upgrades.
Per-operation or time-limited credentials; the one-secret-per-extension-id model stays.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A /ext/pair request for an id that already holds a stored secret is refused without storing or returning any new secret, unless the request presents the prior secret and it matches constant-time. A refused rebind leaves the previous token valid and emits no credential-bearing event.
After a UI trust reset that verifiably removed the stored secret, pairing the same id again takes the fresh-pairing path with today's behavior.

In a debug build without a user decision, a live key remains valid and no new key is issued for an already-paired id; the auto-approve branch is reachable only from the Rust test harness (cfg(test)) and never replaces an existing credential in an ordinary debug run.

The release dialog for a rebind states key replacement and names the extension; for first pairing it keeps the capability-grant description from C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE, and the pairing_grant_description tests are updated to cover the replacement wording.

After an approved rebind, the previous token receives 401 on /ext/context, /ext/apply, /ext/text-insert and the stream routes, with no events emitted (old-token fencing coverage in the style of the existing disable regressions).

Rebind regressions fail before the fix and pass after it: a debug auto-approve that re-keys an already-paired id must fail, and the fresh-pairing, denial and capability-gating tests still pass unchanged in meaning.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: New rebind regressions fail before the fix and pass after it; the grant-description and capability-gating suites still pass; final GRACE assertions and current-state integrity pass before archiving.
